chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from some of his companions from Aban ibn Uthman from a man who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to a man that there was a debt upon him, so he said: 'The man pays what is upon him from his debt, and divides what remains among the heirs.'
ai.seo_question: How are debts handled in Islamic inheritance before distributing the estate to heirs?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the priority of debt repayment in inheritance law, emphasizing that personal liabilities must be settled from the estate before any division among heirs. It reflects the Shia juristic consensus that debts are a claim against the deceased's assets, ensuring creditors' rights are honored prior to the distribution of the residual wealth to beneficiaries.
